title: Grasse and Bouillé 1779: an enciphered war plan for the defence of the French West Indies read

plaintext.source: IREL record: "Autre chiffre préparé par MM. de Bouillé et de Grasse" (no summary); no gloss, no contemporary decipherment found.

transcription.notes: Running text (images 0309-0313) transcribed; the four pages of enciphered tables (0314-0317) are not transcribed.

system.summary: Numerical syllabary/nomenclator of about 850 numbers, homophones, code names for islands

prior_solution.where: IREL record gives no summary; not in the catalogue or targets/; web search negative (checked 28 Oct 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out check fixed in advance, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Bouillé's key K6 (targets/bouille1778, PR #171) extended by aligning three contemporary cipher/plain pairs (ANOM C8 A 79 fols. 3/5, C8 A 81 fols. 212-213, C8 A 81 fols. 55-56) -> K7, 509 values, frozen.

Frozen K7 on a held-out fourth pair (Bouillé's memorandum of 14 Sept 1781, C8 A 80 fols. 113-115, 485 groups, against the contemporary 'Déchiffrement'): 0.825 words / 0.889 characters vs max 0.149 / 0.089 for 200 permuted controls; criterion fixed in advance (characters >= 0.85, words >= 0.75, above controls).
Running text of the 1779 plan read with K8 (K7 + held-out pair).

outcome.method_basis: Bouillé's key rebuilt from glossed sibling letters and contemporary cipher/plain pairs, validated on a held-out pair.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 778/794 words read in their sense (757 certain, 9 probable, 12 restored, 16 unresolved; unresolved groups counted one word per number). Enciphered tables (images 0314-0317) not read.

credits.note: key extended with cipher/plain pairs and validated on a held-out pair; plan read, English translation

texts.label: Grasse and Bouillé, plan for the protection of the French colonies in America, Martinique, 4 Aug 1779
texts.summary: A small mobile squadron (8 ships, 2,500 men) based at Martinique to guard the islands in winter and strike the British elsewhere, from Florida to Newfoundland; Bouillé to command on land, Grasse at sea.
